first.rationale: Both activation and onboarding completion are down this quarter, and two independent inherited memories (memory_31, memory_86) point to signup/onboarding simplification as a durable lever for exactly these metrics in self-serve/SMB accounts. Verifying these two lets me confirm the original experiments actually measured durable, not just short-term, lift before committing my one experiment slot. I'm deliberately not choosing promotional_pricing despite the competitive pressure: matching aggressive entry pricing risks attracting low-quality, price-sensitive accounts that erode long-term qualified revenue (the stated objective), and memory_73 doesn't speak to sustained retention or revenue quality, only acquisition/short-term lift. Enterprise_sales_assist and referral_incentive are not aligned with the acute problems this week. I'm running this as a standard_experiment rather than broad_rollout because even with two consistent prior signals, current-quarter conditions differ (new competitive dynamics could be a confound for the activation/onboarding dip), so I want a real read before scaling. Downstream value risk is flagged because a narrow focus on activation/completion metrics could mask whether simplified onboarding pulls in lower-intent signups that don't convert to qualified revenue, which needs explicit tracking alongside the experiment.

final.rationale: Archive confirms both records. exp_31 (signup simplification, SMB): activation +9%, qualified revenue +4%, but 30-day retention -1% and explicitly not replicated outside SMB. exp_86 (shortened onboarding): completion +13%, time-to-value -2.1 days, retention +3%, confirmed. Together these directly target this quarter's two soft spots (activation -6%, onboarding completion -4%) and the SMB segment under competitive pricing pressure, with a net-positive revenue signal from exp_31 despite the small retention dip. I'm proceeding with simplify_onboarding (combining signup-field reduction and onboarding-flow shortening) rather than promotional_pricing: matching the competitor's price war risks a race-to-the-bottom that attracts low-LTV accounts, and no inherited memory shows durable qualified-revenue benefit from reactive price-matching against aggressive entrants. I'm keeping this a standard_experiment rather than broad_rollout because exp_31's retention -1% and 'not replicated on other segments' caveat mean I should confirm the SMB-specific effect holds again under today's competitive conditions before scaling company-wide. Downstream value risk is flagged specifically because of that retention dip in exp_31 — completion and activation could look great while quietly trading off some retention, so I want qualified-revenue and 90-day retention tracked as guardrail metrics, not just top-line activation/completion. Uncertainty is preserved: this is a confirmed-but-segment-limited pattern re-applied to a new competitive context, not a guaranteed rollout.
